meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Eloy City Council met on Monday, September 14, 2026, at 6:00 PM, with all seven members present. The Council approved the consent agenda 7-0, approved buying a police demonstration truck for up to $80,000 by a 7-0 vote, and adopted emergency Ordinance No. 26-1006 by a 7-0 vote. The ordinance lets the Mayor appoint Councilmembers to fill empty seats on the Building Advisory and Board of Appeals for now.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- **Consent agenda (approved 7-0):** The Council approved these routine items with one vote:
  - Minutes from the August 24, 2026 Council meeting.
  - Proposals from MHQ of Arizona to install emergency equipment in two 2026 Ford F-150 Police Responder trucks, for up to $95,000, under Arizona State Contract #CTR078487.
  - Resolution No. 26-1678, which accepts an $87,100 grant from the Gila River Indian Community for the Eloy Fire District.
- **Police demonstration vehicle (approved 7-0):** The Council approved buying one 2024 Ford F-150 Police Responder demonstration vehicle from San Tan Ford. The truck already has an MHQ emergency equipment package. The cost will not exceed $80,000 under Arizona State Contract CTR 059323, Phase 2. The money comes from Proposition 207, the Smart and Safe Arizona Act, which taxes recreational marijuana.
- **Ordinance No. 26-1006, Building Advisory and Board of Appeals (adopted 7-0, with emergency clause):** This change to Section 2-111 of the City Code lets the Mayor appoint Councilmembers to fill empty seats on the board. Councilmembers appointed this way would be voting members. The Council first agreed by voice vote, with no one opposed, to read the ordinance by title. It then adopted the ordinance and the emergency clause by a 7-0 roll call vote. Because of the emergency clause, it takes effect right away.

### Discussion
- **Police demonstration vehicle**
  - A Councilmember asked why this truck costs less to equip than the two new trucks on the consent agenda. The Police Chief said the equipment, about $28,000 worth, is already in the purchase price. The truck has about 80 to 85 percent of the needed equipment. It only needs small changes to the area used to transport prisoners.
  - The truck will be used by a community service officer. This officer handles non-criminal reports and takes prisoners to jail. The City will own the truck instead of leasing it, and it should last at least four to five years.
  - The Chief said vehicle graphics usually cost about $3,500. The truck will be marked "Community Service Officer."
  - The truck has about 1,500 miles on it. The Chief did not know when its warranty started and offered to find out. He expects it to have the normal manufacturer warranty.
  - The Chief said the City gets about $70,000 a year from Proposition 207.
  - Asked why the City is buying a demonstration vehicle, the Chief said the City's fleet staff learned the truck was already equipped. They saw a chance for big savings.
- **Building Advisory and Board of Appeals**
  - The City Attorney said the five-member board does not have a quorum, meaning enough members to meet. Fewer than three members are active. Staff expect some building code appeals soon, including cases that could involve condemning buildings. If the board cannot meet, the City could face liability.
  - An emergency clause needs a three-fourths vote, or six of seven members. Without it, the ordinance would have taken effect 30 days later.
  - The board works on its own, and the Council does not review its decisions. Appeals go straight to Superior Court within 30 days. The change is meant to be temporary, with one-year terms. Staff will return later for direction on how the board should be made up.
  - Eligibility had already been expanded to people living in Pinal County. The City Manager said the City has advertised for months without any applicants. Filling the board will now be a top priority.
  - Councilmember Galindo said she knew people with construction experience who said they had applied. She also mentioned someone outside Eloy who might be interested. Staff said the job requirements are listed on the application on the City website.
  - Vice Mayor Tarango asked if any qualified applicants had been turned down. Staff said none had been. They added that the City's new Chief Building Official (CBO) will help review candidates. This may allow a wider range of people to serve, since staff will brief the board on each case.
  - A Councilmember asked if a short-term, temporary committee could be used instead. The City Attorney said the Council could choose that. But he was concerned that three to six months would not be enough time, especially over the holidays.
  - Councilmember Vedrasca and Councilmember Galindo said Councilmembers are willing to serve but lack building code expertise. Councilmember Vedrasca asked about training and preparation time. The City Attorney said Councilmembers have experience with complex land use issues. He also said the Planning Director would give appointees an orientation.
  - Councilmember Curtis supported the ordinance as a good short-term fix. She suggested the City consider paying board members in the future. The City Attorney said elected officials cannot receive extra pay beyond what their office allows. He said a stipend, such as for gas money, could be considered for other boards.
  - Mayor Sutton said the board is very important. He believes many people in Eloy and Pinal County could serve if the City gets the word out.
  - The City Attorney said someone was suggested during the meeting as a possible board member.

### Public comments
- A former Maricopa City Councilwoman and Air Force veteran introduced herself as a candidate for office. She described her 20 years of work in veteran services, including at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and the Arizona Department of Veterans' Services.
- She remembered service members lost after September 11. She gave the Mayor a challenge coin with City of Maricopa veterans on one side and the Twin Towers on the other. She also thanked the City for celebrating its traditions at Fiestas Patrias.
- The Mayor thanked her and said he would display the coin in his office.

### Reports and announcements
- **Mayor Sutton:**
  - He congratulated the Eloy Dust Devils football team on wins over St. John's on September 4 and over Tombstone the following Friday.
  - He opened the 75th annual Fiestas Patrias. A former Eloy Mayor served as Grand Marshal, joined by many past Grand Marshals. He thanked Corazon de Latinos Unidos (CDLU) for running the two-day event.
  - He praised the Sun Corridor Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) for its Safe Routes to School booth. At the booth, children showed how they get to school and how they would like to get there.
- **Councilmember Vedrasca:** He said he was glad to be back after being away since August 23.
- **Councilmember Galindo:**
  - She attended a Pinal County Board of Supervisors meeting where a solar farm at Phillips and Sunshine was approved. The Board also approved a proclamation for Suicide Awareness and Prevention Month.
  - She announced a suicide prevention and remembrance event by the Sparrow campaign on Saturday night at Santa Cruz High School.
  - For CDLU, she thanked Community Services staff and all volunteers. She thanked the City for being the event's premier sponsor through services and money. She also thanked staff for installing new sidewalk ramps in time for the event, which helped people with limited mobility.
  - She congratulated Councilmember Curtis and her team on winning first place in the parade.
- **Councilmember Garcia:** He attended the Pinal Partnership meeting and will attend the Steps of Love event on Saturday. He reminded residents that school fall break starts Thursday and asked drivers to watch for children.
- **Councilmember Snyder:**
  - He attended the Pinal Partnership meeting, where Arizona State University presented a computer decision-making tool that uses artificial intelligence (AI). The tool pulls together data from sources such as the Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT), the state revenue department, and schools.
  - It can show the effects of choices like moving a road or changes in inflation. He said the tool will be available to small cities like Eloy with limited staff.
- **City Manager:**
  - He thanked staff and CDLU for Fiestas Patrias, a large free community event.
  - **Fantastic Fridays, Pizza Palooza:** Friday, September 18, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Troy Thomas Community Center, for ages 5 to 12. Space is limited.
  - **Top Notch Teens painting class:** Friday, September 25, from 6 to 8:30 p.m., for ages 11 to 17, led by a local artist. About 12 to 15 spots are available.
  - To register for either event, visit the Community Services building downtown or apply online.
  - National Child Passenger Safety Week is September 20 to 26. The Police Department will help teach parents and caregivers how to install car seats correctly. He noted that about 45 percent of car seats are installed incorrectly.
- The meeting adjourned by voice vote.
